about: translationCore 4 design-system baseline. Each case is one component in one state inside a fixed-size frame; screens/<component>/<state>.png is how tC4 draws it. A port renders the same case by the same protocol and compares images.

protocol.page: Load src/ds/styles.css (every token file and @font-face). Set <html lang> and <html dir> from the case's `document`. Size the viewport to the frame (device scale factor 1). The body has margin 0 and the frame's background.
protocol.frame: A <div data-case="<id>" tabindex="-1"> at the top-left corner of the page: box-sizing border-box, the frame's width, height, padding and background, overflow hidden. The case renders inside it. Because the viewport is the frame, a Layer's fixed scrim covers exactly the frame and an anchored popover measures the frame as its window.
protocol.fonts: Load every @font-face of the stylesheet before mounting, then wait for document.fonts.ready.
protocol.pointerFirst: Before mounting, click the pointer at (1, 1), inside the frame's padding. The click gives the empty frame the focus without a focus ring, as a click on the button that opens a dialog does in the app, so a component that moves the focus by script on mount (Modal, Drawer and ConfirmDialog focus their first control) shows no ring either: Chromium draws a ring on script focus only when the element that had the focus showed one, or when nothing had the focus. The pointer stays at (1, 1) unless a step moves it.

steps.focus: Press Tab until the first element inside the frame that matches `target` has the focus. Keyboard focus is what makes :focus-visible match.
steps.hover: Move the pointer to the centre of the first element inside the frame that matches `target`.
steps.press: Move the pointer to the centre of the target and press the primary button without releasing it (:active).
steps.click: Click the centre of the target.
steps.type: Type `text` into the focused element, one key at a time.

protocol.motion: Every CSS transition and animation is off (as if finished; an infinite animation shows its element without the animation). The text caret is hidden.
protocol.settle: After mounting wait 150 ms, and after each step 300 ms, then for document.fonts.ready, for every image to decode, and for two animation frames. Then screenshot the frame element.
protocol.output: screens/<component>/<state>.png, the frame element only, 1 CSS px = 1 image px.

nodes.element: { "$el": "<Name>", "props": { ... } } — a DS export (index.js) when the name is capitalised, an HTML or SVG tag when it is lower case. `children` is a prop.
nodes.callback: { "$fn": "noop" } — a callback that does nothing. Several components draw a control only when they are given a callback (Modal's ✕, Toast's action, Breadcrumb's links, a clickable Surface).
nodes.asset: { "$asset": "<path>" } — a file of the tC4 checkout, by its path relative to the checkout, served as a URL.
nodes.json: Everything else is a plain JSON value. Style objects are React inline styles: camelCase properties, a bare number means px except on unitless properties (lineHeight, flex, opacity, fontWeight, zIndex). defaultValue is the initial value of an uncontrolled field.
nodes.cell: { "$cell": "<name>" } — the current value of a cell of the case's `cells`. A write draws the case again with the new value, as a parent's state would.
nodes.set: { "$fn": "set", "cell": "<name>", "value": <json> } or { "$fn": "set", "cell": "<name>", "from": "<path>" } — a callback that writes the cell: `value`, or the value at `from` in the callback's arguments ("0" is the first argument, "0.target.checked" the checked state of the first argument's target, "0.id" the id field of a table row).
nodes.render: When `render` is absent the case renders { "$el": component, "props": props }. When it is present it is the whole tree, and the component under test sits inside it with exactly `props`.
